{"id":"mimid-1wgh.138","title":"The mimid service surface: verbs for what IRC cannot say","description":"Mark 2026-11-27: "i would really like to add a bunch of quote mimi foo bar to the irc agent", and on being shown the four candidates, all four.

THE MECHANISM ALREADY EXISTS. Mark asked for the raw verb on 2026-11-22: crates/mimid-agent-irc/src/service.rs handles both /msg mimid <command> and MIMID <command>, one handler, NOTICEs from mimid!mimid@<server>. Seventeen commands are on it. So this epic adds verbs, not plumbing.

THE LINE TO HOLD, which the existing surface already follows: a real IRC verb where the data fits IRC's shape, which is why rooms are JOIN and PART, and the service only where MIMI has a concept IRC lacks. Stock clients parse MODE and NAMES replies and are confused by unexpected content; a NOTICE is text they print. Every command here is in the second class, and a reviewer should check that claim before building one.

THE REPLY PATH MATTERS. service.rs records why the service nick is the documented path: its NOTICEs land in a query window a client renders and logs, while a raw-verb reply can land in a status window a client renders oddly or discards. Anything whose output a user must read carefully says so in its help text.

SMALL ITEM, not worth its own bead: MIMI as an alias for the MIMID verb, since Mark's muscle memory says "quote mimi". Whichever child lands first adds it, with both names in help.

WHAT THE CODE ADMITS TODAY, from service.rs's Limitations: "reports and removing participants have no command in v1". Two of the four children close exactly that sentence, which must be rewritten when they do.

EACH CHILD MUST: add the command to the handler and to the doc-comment table that is the surface's reference; extend the help output; cover it in docs/design/agent-frontends.md §4 and §7.5; and test the command, its bad input and its refusal. The commands run after registration on an authenticated connection, so the credential check of docs/design/frontend-auth.md §4.1 has already happened and none of them re-checks it; a command that acts outside this user's own account would be a new boundary and does not belong here.

{"notes":"CORRECTION to this epic's own rule, 2026-11-27, prompted by Mark asking which standard IRC verbs return metadata and status and whether mimid answers them.

The epic said every command here is in the second class, a MIMI concept IRC lacks. One was not. The agent's own state — groups out of sync, outbox depth, last sync, the carrier's agreed intervals — was planned as a service subcommand called status, and IRC already has the verb for it: STATS, whose letters are server-defined and which /stats reaches in every client. It moved to bead mimid-1wgh.138.1 with TIME, INFO and HELP, under this epic's rule rather than against it.

That bead also records what mimid answers today and what it does not, and which of the missing verbs are deliberately not worth adding for a single-user agent.

HELP changes this epic's shape slightly: with a service surface this size, nothing leads a user to it, so the help text needs one source that both the service nick and the HELP verb read."}
